newsitem.title: THAILAND: Standard Chartered confident on Thai economy.
newsitem.headline: Standard Chartered confident on Thai economy.

text.p: Britain's Standard Chartered Bank remains optimistic about Thailand's economic fundamentals, saying fears that the country's economy had deteriorated to dangerous levels were exaggerated.

"The Thai financial system is under some strain but rumours of Thailand's demise are much exaggerated," the bank's Group Chief Executive Malcolm Williamson said at a British Chamber of Commerce function in Bangkok on Monday.
"At a macro level, the Thai economy remains quite robust," he said, adding: "I believe Thai banks and financial institutions will develop into regional powerhouses in a global context."
Thailand's economy has sunk to its worst position in 10 years, hit by sluggish exports, a crippled property sector, a continued decline in its stock market and a troubled banking and finance sector.
The country's economic woes have sparked heavy foreign selling of Thai shares, particularly bank stocks, and recent calls by some Thai politicians for Finance Minister Amnuay Viravan to step down.
Standard Chartered sees Thailand as one of its targets for expansion in Asia, outside of Hong Kong. The bank recently opened a large new country headquarters in Thailand.

"Though the star may have slipped a little it certainly hasn't dropped from the sky...this country is by no means facing the sort of problems that were facing Mexico a few years ago," Williamson said.
Dru Narwani, Chief Executive for Standard Chartered in Thailand, said he expected the economy to bottom in six to nine months.

Private economists forecast gross domestic product will grow about five percent this year, down from 6.7 percent in 1996 and 8.6 percent in 1995. The central bank says it expects the economy to grow at least six percent in 1997.
